title: Find out the year the house was built (pre-1978 = assume lead paint)
check: Record build year in Hearth house notes. If before 1978, any job that disturbs painted surfaces uses a lead-safe certified contractor or lead-safe DIY practices.
cite: US EPA, Lead-Safe Renovations for DIYers (RRP)
quote: If your home was built before 1978, it may have lead-based paint

title: Test suspect materials before demolition (asbestos)
check: Before tearing out old flooring, popcorn ceilings, duct wrap or insulation, have an accredited professional sample them. Undisturbed, intact material can be left alone.
cite: US EPA, Protect Your Family from Exposures to Asbestos
quote: You are planning to remodel your home (remodeling can disturb building materials)

title: Plan smoke-alarm upgrades whenever a permit is pulled
check: Any permitted interior alteration triggers smoke alarms to new-construction locations for the dwelling. Budget the alarms into the first interior project, not the last.
cite: 2021 IRC R314.2.2 Alterations, Repairs and Additions
quote: Where alterations , repairs or additions requiring a permit occur, the individual dwelling unit shall be equipped with smoke alarms located as required for new dwellings

title: Plan CO-alarm upgrades on the same trigger
check: Same permit trigger applies to carbon monoxide alarms (exterior-only work such as roofing/siding/windows is exempt).
cite: 2021 IRC R315.2.2 Alterations, Repairs and Additions
quote: Where alterations , repairs or additions requiring a permit occur, the individual dwelling unit shall be equipped with carbon monoxide alarms located as required for new dwellings

title: Locate and label the main water shutoff
check: Find the main shutoff near where the water service enters; confirm it is accessible and fully opens/closes. Photo it into Hearth before any plumbing work.
quote: Each dwelling unit shall be provided with an accessible main shutoff valve near the entrance of the water service

title: Locate the service disconnect and panel; check working space
check: Clear 36 in. of working space in front of the panel; record the main breaker rating on the label.
cite: 2021 IRC E3405.2 Working Clearances for Energized Equipment and Panelboards
quote: the dimension of the working space in the direction of access to panelboards and live parts of other equipment likely to require examination, adjustment, servicing or maintenance while energized shall be not less than 36 inches (914 mm) in depth

title: Dry any water damage within 24-48 hours before closing walls
check: If demolition exposes wet framing or drywall, dry it within 24-48 h; mold areas over ~10 sq ft need a remediation plan, not a DIY wipe.
cite: US EPA, A Brief Guide to Mold, Moisture and Your Home
quote: It is important to dry water-damaged areas and items within 24-48 hours to prevent mold growth

title: Inspect floors, walls, ceilings, stairs and a sample of doors/windows
check: Walk each room: open/close doors and windows, note fogged double-pane glass (broken seals), loose rails or wide baluster gaps.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.10
quote: any window that was obviously fogged or displayed other evidence of broken seals

title: Look for signs of foundation movement before cosmetic work
check: Sheetrock cracks, out-of-square door frames and unlevel floors point to structure first; resolve before new finishes.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.3
quote: observed indications of possible foundation movement, such as sheetrock cracks, brick cracks, out-of-square door frames, and unlevel floors

title: Survey existing kitchen: shutoffs under sink and at dishwasher
check: Each fixture/appliance supply needs its own accessible shutoff; note any missing under the sink, at the dishwasher and fridge ice line.
cite: 2021 IRC P2903.9.3 Fixture Valves and Access
quote: Shutoff valves shall be required on each fixture supply pipe to each plumbing appliance and to each plumbing fixture other than bathtubs and showers

title: Test countertop receptacles for GFCI protection
check: Press TEST/RESET on every countertop receptacle (or its upstream GFCI). Any countertop outlet without GFCI protection is a fix item.
quote: 125-volt through 250-volt receptacles that serve countertop surfaces and are supplied by single-phase branch circuits rated 150 volts or less to ground shall have ground -fault circuit-interrupter protection for personnel

title: Check receptacles within 6 ft of the sink
check: Every receptacle within 6 ft of the sink bowl edge needs GFCI protection (includes non-countertop ones).
quote: 125-volt through 250-volt receptacles that are located within 6 feet (1829 mm) of the top inside edge of the bowl of the sink

title: Check for leaks and functional drainage at the sink
check: Run water, fill and drain the sink; look for active leaks in the cabinet base.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.6
quote: active plumbing water leaks that were observed during the inspection

title: Decide layout: countertop runs and island/peninsula
check: Count every countertop wall space 12 in. or wider; each needs receptacles so no point is more than 24 in. from one. Lock the layout before electrical rough-in.
quote: Receptacle outlets shall be installed so that no point along the wall line is more than 24 inches (610 mm), measured horizontally, from a receptacle outlet in that space

title: Plan at least two 20-A small-appliance circuits
check: Confirm with the electrician that countertop/dining receptacles are on two or more 20-A circuits.
cite: 2021 IRC E3703.2 Kitchen and Dining Area Receptacles
quote: A minimum of two 20-ampere-rated branch circuits shall be provided for all receptacle outlets specified by Section E3901.3

title: Decide range hood: ducted to outdoors, rated airflow
check: Ducted hoods must exit outdoors (never attic/crawl space) through a smooth, airtight duct with a backdraft damper.
quote: Domestic cooking exhaust equipment shall discharge to the outdoors through a duct

title: Check minimum kitchen exhaust rate
check: Pick a hood that meets at least 100 cfm intermittent (or 25 cfm continuous).
quote: Kitchens 100 cfm intermittent or 25 cfm continuous

title: Large hood (>400 cfm) with non-direct-vent gas appliances = makeup air
check: If the hood exceeds 400 cfm and the house has atmospheric gas appliances, plan makeup air.
quote: each exhaust system capable of exhausting in excess of 400 cubic feet per minute (0.19 m 3 /s) shall be mechanically or passively provided with makeup air

title: Hood duct material
check: Specify galvanized steel, stainless or copper duct for the hood run (PVC only for qualifying downdraft under slab).
quote: Ducts serving domestic cooking exhaust equipment shall be constructed of galvanized steel, stainless steel or copper

title: Dishwasher circuit GFCI
check: Verify the dishwasher branch circuit/outlet is GFCI protected.
cite: 2021 IRC E3902.11 Kitchen Dishwasher Branch Circuit
quote: Ground -fault circuit-interrupter protection shall be provided for outlets supplied by branch circuits rated 150 volts or less to ground that supply dishwashers

title: AFCI on kitchen 15/20-A outlet circuits
check: Kitchen outlet circuits need AFCI protection (combination AFCI breaker or approved method).
cite: 2021 IRC E3902.20 Arc-Fault Circuit Interrupter Protection
quote: Branch circuits that supply 120-volt, single-phase, 15- and 20-ampere outlets installed in kitchens

title: Dishwasher backflow: air gap or approved preventer
check: Confirm an air gap (counter or integral) or backflow preventer on the dishwasher supply.
cite: 2021 IRC P2717.1 Protection of Water Supply
quote: The water supply to a dishwasher shall be protected against backflow by an air gap

title: Dishwasher drain high loop
check: Drain hose/tube must rise to the underside of the counter before connecting to the disposer or tailpiece.
quote: The dishwasher discharge pipe or tubing shall rise to the underside of the counter and be fastened or otherwise held in that position

title: Water hammer arrestors for quick-closing valves
check: Dishwashers and ice makers use quick-closing valves; add arrestors at rough-in.
quote: A water-hammer arrestor shall be installed where quick-closing valves are utilized

title: Pressure-test new supply piping before closing walls
check: Ask for the water-supply test (working pressure, or 50 psi air for non-plastic, held 15 min) before drywall.
quote: This pressure shall be held for not less than 15 minutes

title: Countertop receptacle height
check: Receptacles must be no more than 20 in. above the counter (or listed in-counter assemblies).
quote: On or above, but not more than 20 inches (508 mm) above, the countertop or work surface

title: Record new appliances into Hearth inventory
check: Add range, hood, dishwasher, fridge, disposal with model/serial/receipt/warranty end (inventory categories 1-7).
cite: Insurance Information Institute, Home inventory brochure
quote: whenever you make a significant purchase, remember to add the information to your inventory

title: Flush every toilet; check for rocking or leaks at the floor
check: Loose or leaking toilets at the flange get fixed before new flooring.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.6
quote: toilets that were damaged, had loose connections to the floor, were leaking, or had tank components that did not operate

title: Test bathroom receptacles for GFCI
check: Every bathroom receptacle must be GFCI protected.
quote: 125-volt through 250-volt receptacles installed in bathrooms and supplied by single-phase branch circuits rated 150 volts or less to ground shall have ground -fault circuit-interrupter protection for personnel

title: Confirm exhaust fan vents outdoors (not into attic)
check: Trace the fan duct in the attic; termination inside the attic is a defect.
quote: Exhaust air from bathrooms , toilet rooms and kitchens shall not discharge into an attic , crawl space or other areas inside the building

title: Check tub/shower glass for safety glazing marks
check: Glass within 60 in. of the standing surface at tubs/showers is a hazardous location; look for the tempered/safety etch.
cite: 2021 IRC R308.4.5 Glazing and Wet Surfaces
quote: Glazing in walls , enclosures or fences containing or adjacent to hot tubs, spas, whirlpools, saunas, steam rooms, bathtubs, showers

title: Ventilation: window or fan sized to code
check: Without a 3 sq ft window (half openable) you need a fan: 50 cfm intermittent or 20 cfm continuous.
quote: Mechanical exhaust capacity of 50 cfm intermittent or 20 cfm

title: Dedicated 20-A bathroom receptacle circuit
check: Plan at least one 20-A circuit for bathroom receptacles with no other outlets.
quote: A minimum of one 20-ampere branch circuit shall be provided to supply bathroom receptacle outlet (s)

title: Receptacle within 36 in. of each basin
check: Place a receptacle within 36 in. of the outside edge of each lavatory basin.
quote: such outlet shall be located within 36 inches (914 mm) of the outside edge of each lavatory basin

title: Shower valve type: pressure-balance or thermostatic
check: Specify a balanced-pressure, thermostatic or combination valve rated for the shower head flow.
quote: Individual shower and tub/shower combination valves shall be balanced-pressure, thermostatic or combination balanced-pressure/thermostatic valves

title: Tub-only valve: temperature limit 120 F
check: Tub (non-shower) valves need a temperature-limiting device capped at 120 F.
cite: 2021 IRC P2713.3 Bathtub and Whirlpool Bathtub Valves
quote: equipped with a means to limit the maximum setting of the device to 120°F (49°C)

title: Ceiling height check before soffits or lowered ceilings
check: Bathrooms need at least 6 ft 8 in. ceiling height.
quote: Bathrooms , toilet rooms and laundry rooms shall have a ceiling height of not less than 6 feet 8 inches (2032 mm)

title: Tile backer board: listed material only (not plain drywall)
check: Behind tub/shower tile use listed backers (cement board, fiber-cement, glass-mat gypsum, etc.).
quote: Materials used as backers for wall tile in tub and shower areas and wall panels in shower areas shall be of materials listed in Table R702.4.2

title: Built-up shower pan liner or bonded membrane
check: On-site shower receptors need a liner (PVC/CPE, lead, copper, hot mop or ANSI A118.10 membrane). Ask for the flood test before tile.
quote: The adjoining walls and floor framing enclosing on-site built-up shower receptors shall be lined with one of the following materials

title: Shower riser anchored
check: Supply riser from valve to head must be secured to framing.
quote: Water supply risers from the shower valve to the shower head outlet , whether exposed or concealed , shall be attached to the structure

title: DWV test at rough-in
check: Drain/waste/vent rough-in gets a water or air test without leakage before walls close.
quote: DWV systems shall be tested on completion of the rough piping installation

title: Nonabsorbent finish to 6 ft above the floor
check: Shower walls and tub walls with a shower head: nonabsorbent finish at least 6 ft high.
cite: 2021 IRC R307.2 Bathtub and Shower Spaces
quote: Such wall surfaces shall extend to a height of not less than 6 feet (1829 mm) above the floor

title: Receptacles near tub/shower stall
check: Any receptacle within 6 ft of the tub or shower edge needs GFCI.
cite: 2021 IRC E3902.8 Bathtub or Shower Stall Receptacles
quote: located within 6 feet (1829 mm) of the outside edge of a bathtub or shower stall

title: Fixtures secured and supported
check: Toilet bolted to flange/floor with corrosion-resistant fasteners; wall-hung fixtures rigidly supported.
quote: Floor- outlet or floor-mounted fixtures shall be secured to the drainage connection and to the floor

title: Receptacle spacing along walls
check: Check that general receptacles exist along usable walls (no point along the floor line more than 6 ft from one). Note gaps before new flooring/trim.
quote: no point measured horizontally along the floor line of any wall space is more than 6 feet (1829 mm), from a receptacle outlet

title: Fireplace: damper, hearth, and alarms in the room
check: Open/close the damper; look for cracks at hearth/extension; confirm smoke and CO alarms in that room.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.8
quote: the lack of a carbon monoxide detector in the same room as the fireplace

title: Stair geometry, handrails and guards
check: Measure risers: max 7-3/4 in., and no riser in a flight more than 3/8 in. taller than the shortest.
quote: The riser height shall be not more than 7 3 / 4 inches (196 mm)

title: Guards at open sides
check: Open-sided walking surfaces more than 30 in. above the floor below need guards (at least 36 in. high per R312.1.2).
quote: located more than 30 inches (762 mm) measured vertically to the floor or grade below

title: Handrail height
check: Handrails 34-38 in. above the tread nosing line; required on flights with 4+ risers (R311.7.8).
quote: shall be not less than 34 inches (864 mm) and not more than 38 inches (965 mm)

title: Window/door glass near doors and floors = safety glazing
check: When replacing windows near doors or low to the floor, confirm safety glazing where required.
cite: 2021 IRC R308.4.2 Glazing Adjacent to Doors
quote: Glazing in an individual fixed or operable panel adjacent to a door shall be considered to be a hazardous location

title: Natural light and ventilation in habitable rooms
check: If enlarging walls or closing windows, keep glazing at least 8% and openable area at least 4% of floor area (or mechanical ventilation).
quote: Habitable rooms shall have an aggregate glazing area of not less than 8 percent of the floor area of such rooms

title: Ceiling height for any new or finished space
check: Habitable spaces and hallways need at least 7 ft ceiling height.
quote: Habitable space , hallways and portions of basements containing these spaces shall have a ceiling height of not less than 7 feet (2134 mm)

title: AFCI for living/family/dining rooms
check: New or extended outlet circuits in living areas need AFCI protection.
cite: 2021 IRC E3902.20 Arc-Fault Circuit Interrupter Protection
quote: family rooms, dining rooms, living rooms, parlors, libraries, dens, bedrooms

title: Fireblocking at new framing and soffits
check: New stud walls, soffits and chases need fireblocking at concealed draft openings.
quote: fireblocking shall be provided to cut off both vertical and horizontal concealed draft openings

title: Stair lighting with switches at each level
check: Stairs need a light; a wall switch at each floor level where there are 6+ risers.
quote: There shall be a wall switch at each floor level to control the light source where the stairway has six or more risers

title: Faceplates seated and complete
check: All switch and outlet faceplates installed, covering the opening and seated to the finished wall.
quote: Faceplates provided for snap switches , dimmers and control devices mounted in boxes and other enclosures shall be installed so as to completely cover the opening

title: Emergency escape opening in every sleeping room
check: Each bedroom needs at least one operable egress window or door to outside. Do not block or replace with a smaller unit.
cite: 2021 IRC R310.1 Emergency Escape and Rescue Opening Required
quote: Basements , habitable attics and every sleeping room shall have not less than one operable emergency escape and rescue opening

title: Measure the egress window clear opening
check: Net clear opening at least 5.7 sq ft (5.0 sq ft at grade floor), at least 24 in. high and 20 in. wide.
quote: Emergency escape and rescue openings shall have a net clear opening of not less than 5.7 square feet

title: Smoke alarm in each bedroom and outside sleeping areas
check: Confirm an alarm in each sleeping room and in the hall outside; test each.
quote: In each sleeping room. Outside each separate sleeping area in the immediate vicinity of the bedrooms

title: CO alarm outside sleeping areas
check: CO alarm in the hallway outside bedrooms; inside the bedroom if a fuel-burning appliance is in it or its bath.
quote: Carbon monoxide alarms in dwelling units shall be installed outside of each separate sleeping area in the immediate vicinity of the bedrooms

title: Window fall protection on upper floors
check: Upper-floor operable windows with sill under 24 in. and more than 72 in. above grade need opening limits or fall-prevention devices.
quote: where the bottom of the clear opening of an operable window opening is located less than 24 inches (610 mm) above the finished floor and greater than 72 inches (1829 mm) above the finished grade

title: AFCI for bedroom circuits
check: Bedroom outlet circuits need AFCI.
cite: 2021 IRC E3902.20 Arc-Fault Circuit Interrupter Protection
quote: dens, bedrooms, sunrooms

title: Closet light fixture clearances
check: Closet luminaires must keep clearance from the storage space (defined zone to 6 ft or highest rod, 24 in. from walls).
cite: 2021 IRC E4003.12 Luminaires in Clothes-Closet Storage Space
quote: storage space shall be defined as a volume bounded by the sides and back closet walls

title: Dryer duct terminates outdoors
check: Trace the dryer duct to an exterior hood; no termination in attic, crawl or garage; at least 3 ft from openings unless the manufacturer says otherwise.
quote: Exhaust ducts shall terminate on the outside of the building

title: Dryer duct length and joints
check: Max 35 ft minus fitting allowances (unless manufacturer allows more); joints not screwed through more than 1/8 in.
quote: The maximum length of the exhaust duct shall be 35 feet (10 668 mm)

title: GFCI on laundry receptacles
check: Laundry area receptacles need GFCI.
quote: 125-volt through 250-volt receptacles installed in laundry areas

title: Dedicated 20-A laundry circuit
check: At least one 20-A circuit serving only laundry-area receptacles.
quote: A minimum of one 20-ampere-rated branch circuit shall be provided for receptacle outlets required by Section E3901.8

title: Dryer duct installation details
check: Support at most every 12 ft, insert ends in airflow direction, seal and mechanically fasten joints.
quote: Exhaust ducts shall be supported at intervals not to exceed 12 feet (3658 mm)

title: Laundry room ceiling height
check: Laundry rooms need at least 6 ft 8 in.
quote: Bathrooms , toilet rooms and laundry rooms shall have a ceiling height of not less than 6 feet 8 inches

title: AFCI covers laundry areas
check: Laundry outlet circuits are in the AFCI list.
cite: 2021 IRC E3902.20 Arc-Fault Circuit Interrupter Protection
quote: closets , hallways, laundry areas and similar rooms

title: Dryer duct provided even if no dryer yet
check: If a dryer space exists, install the duct; cap and label 'future use' if no dryer at occupancy.
quote: Where space for a clothes dryer is provided, an exhaust duct system shall be installed

title: House-to-garage door rating and self-closer
check: Door from garage to house: 1-3/8 in. solid wood/steel or 20-minute rated, self-latching and self-closing. No openings into bedrooms.
quote: Openings from a private garage directly into a room used for sleeping purposes shall not be permitted

title: Garage-to-house fire separation (drywall)
check: Check that the separation wall/ceiling drywall per Table R302.6 is intact (no holes, unsealed penetrations).
quote: The garage shall be separated as required by Table R302.6

title: GFCI on garage receptacles
check: All garage receptacles GFCI protected.
cite: 2021 IRC E3902.2 Garage and Accessory Building Receptacles
quote: 125-volt through 250-volt receptacles installed in garages

title: Garage door opener safety sensors
check: Test the photo-eye reversal; failed sensors are a correction item.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.10
quote: photo-electric safety sensors that did not operate properly

title: Gas water heater/furnace ignition at 18 in.
check: Fuel-fired appliances in the garage need ignition source at least 18 in. above the floor (unless FVIR listed).
cite: 2021 IRC M1307.3 Elevation of Ignition Source
quote: Appliances having an ignition source shall be elevated such that the source of ignition is not less than 18 inches (457 mm) above the floor in garages

title: Receptacle in each vehicle bay
check: Plan at least one receptacle per bay, not more than 5.5 ft above the floor (EV charger is separate).
cite: 2021 IRC E3901.9 Basements, Garages and Accessory Buildings
quote: in each vehicle bay not more than 5.5 feet (1676 mm) above the floor in attached garages

title: Floor slope and surface for any new slab
check: New garage floors noncombustible and sloped toward a drain or the vehicle door.
quote: The area of floor used for parking of automobiles or other vehicles shall be sloped to facilitate the movement of liquids

title: Roof from ground or eaves: covering, gutters, flashing, penetrations
check: Record roof material and look for missing shingles, lifted flashing at vents/chimney/skylights, and gutter overflow stains.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.1
quote: the roof-covering materials; the gutters; the downspouts; the vents, flashing, skylights, chimney, and other roof penetrations

title: Grading slopes away from the foundation
check: Check grade falls at least 6 in. in the first 10 ft; regrade before siding or foundation work.
quote: The grade shall fall not fewer than 6 inches (152 mm) within the first 10 feet (3048 mm)

title: Exterior walls, trim, windows, doors, decks and railings
check: Walk the perimeter: siding, eaves/soffit/fascia, flashing and trim, steps, decks, guard spacing.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.2
quote: the exterior wall-covering materials; the eaves, soffits and fascia; a representative number of windows; all exterior doors; flashing and trim

title: Outdoor receptacles front and back, GFCI
check: At least one grade-accessible outdoor receptacle at front and back; all outdoor receptacles GFCI.
quote: shall be installed outdoors at the front and back of each dwelling unit having direct access to grade level

title: Wood near soil (rot/termite risk)
check: Wood framing within code distances of soil must be treated or durable; report wood-soil contact.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.3
quote: observed indications of wood in contact with or near soil

title: Landings at exterior doors
check: Each exterior door needs a landing at least as wide as the door and 36 in. deep, max 2% slope.
cite: 2021 IRC R311.3 Floors and Landings at Exterior Doors
quote: There shall be a landing or floor on each side of each exterior door

title: Reroof: tear-off to deck
check: Replacement means removing existing layers to the deck (adhered ice barrier may stay).
quote: Roof replacement shall include the removal of existing layers of roof coverings down to the roof deck

title: Replace rusted/damaged flashings and vents at reroof
check: Do not reuse deteriorated flashing, edging, outlets or vents.
quote: Any existing flashings, edgings, outlets , vents or similar devices that are a part of the assembly shall be replaced where rusted, damaged or deteriorated

title: Shingle slope limits and double underlayment
check: Asphalt shingles only at 2:12 or steeper; 2:12 to 4:12 needs double underlayment.
quote: Asphalt shingles shall be used only on roof slopes of 2 units vertical in 12 units horizontal

title: Roof fire classification
check: Where your jurisdiction requires Class A/B/C roofing (or roof edge within 3 ft of lot line), specify listed covering.
quote: Class A, B or C roofing shall be installed in jurisdictions designated by law as requiring their use

title: Deck lumber: treated or naturally durable
check: New decks: No. 2 or better, preservative-treated or naturally durable lumber.
quote: Wood materials shall be No. 2 grade or better lumber, preservative-treated

title: Drip edge at eaves and rakes
check: Drip edge overlapped 2 in., fastened at most 12 in. o.c.
quote: A drip edge shall be provided at eaves and rake edges of shingle roofs

title: Shingle fastening count
check: At least 4 fasteners per strip shingle (or manufacturer minimum if higher).
quote: not less than four fasteners per strip shingle or two fasteners per individual shingle

title: Wall flashing shingle-fashion at windows and doors
check: When residing or replacing windows, flashing laps shingle-fashion to shed water.
quote: Approved corrosion-resistant flashing shall be applied shingle-fashion

title: Deck ledger attachment
check: Ledger at least 2x8 treated and properly attached to the house band; no concentrated beam loads on it.
quote: Deck ledgers shall be a minimum 2-inch by 8-inch (51 mm by 203 mm) nominal

title: Irrigation backflow
check: Lawn irrigation supply needs a vacuum breaker or RP assembly.
quote: The potable water supply to lawn irrigation systems shall be protected against backflow

title: Active water penetration
check: Look for efflorescence, stains, standing water; report active penetration before finishing.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.3
quote: observed indications of active water penetration

title: GFCI on basement receptacles
check: Basement receptacles GFCI protected (dedicated alarm receptacle exception).
quote: 125-volt through 250-volt receptacles installed in basements

title: Egress for basement bedrooms
check: Any new basement sleeping room needs its own egress opening.
cite: 2021 IRC R310.1 Emergency Escape and Rescue Opening Required
quote: Where basements contain one or more sleeping rooms, an emergency escape and rescue opening shall be required in each sleeping room

title: Smoke alarm on every story including basement
check: Finishing a basement: smoke alarm on that level.
quote: On each additional story of the dwelling , including basements and habitable attics

title: Foundation dampproofing on any excavation
check: When excavating for egress wells or repairs, dampproof walls that retain earth.
cite: 2021 IRC R406.1 Concrete and Masonry Foundation Dampproofing
quote: foundation walls that retain earth and enclose interior spaces and floors below grade shall be dampproofed

title: Unvented crawl space vapor retarder
check: Unvented crawls: continuous Class I vapor retarder, seams lapped 6 in. and taped, up the stem wall 6 in.
quote: Exposed earth shall be covered with a continuous Class I vapor retarder

title: Wood decay protection near ground
check: Wood framing near exposed ground (e.g., joists within 18 in.) must be treated or durable.
quote: wood joists or the bottom of a wood structural floor where closer than 18 inches (457 mm) to exposed ground

title: Service entrance, panel and breakers walk-through
check: Inspector-style check: service drop, meter, main disconnect, panelboard, grounding/bonding, open knockouts.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.7
quote: any unused circuit-breaker panel opening that was not filled

title: Solid aluminum branch wiring
check: Look for solid-conductor aluminum branch wiring; if present, get an electrician's remediation plan before adding circuits.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.7
quote: the presence of solid conductor aluminum branch-circuit wiring, if readily visible

title: Dedicated space above/below panel kept clear
check: No pipes or ducts in the panel's dedicated space (width/depth of panel, floor to 6 ft above).
cite: 2021 IRC E3405.3 Indoor Dedicated Panelboard Space
quote: Piping, ducts , leak protection apparatus and other equipment foreign to the electrical installation shall not be installed in such dedicated space

title: Water heater: venting, TPR valve, seismic bracing
check: Check vent connection, TPR valve and discharge pipe, and strapping where required.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.6
quote: the water heating equipment, including the energy source, venting connections, temperature/pressure-relief (TPR) valves, Watts 210 valves, and seismic bracing

title: TPR discharge pipe routing
check: Discharge full size to an air gap in the same room; not connected directly to drains.
cite: 2021 IRC P2804.6.1 Requirements for Discharge Pipe
quote: Discharge through an air gap located in the same room as the water heater

title: Water heater pan where leaks cause damage
check: Tank heaters over finished space need a pan at least 1-1/2 in. deep with a 3/4 in. drain.
cite: 2021 IRC P2801.6.1 Pan Size and Drain
quote: The pan shall be not less than 1 1 / 2 inches (38 mm) deep

title: Water heater in garage: ignition elevation
check: Gas heaters in garages: ignition source at least 18 in. above floor unless FVIR-listed.
cite: 2021 IRC P2801.7 Water Heaters Installed in Garages
quote: Water heaters having an ignition source shall be elevated such that the source of ignition is not less than 18 inches (457 mm) above the garage floor

title: Run heat and cooling with normal controls
check: Confirm both systems operate from the thermostat; record thermostat location and system type.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.4
quote: the location of the thermostat for the heating system; the energy source; and the heating method

title: Attic insulation depth and ventilation
check: Record insulation type and approximate depth; note absent ventilation or insulation.
cite: InterNACHI Home Inspection Standards of Practice §3.9
quote: the general absence of insulation or ventilation in unfinished spaces

title: Attic access opening
check: Attics with 30 in.+ headroom over 30 sq ft need an access at least 22x30 in.
quote: The rough-framed opening shall be not less than 22 inches by 30 inches

title: Grounding electrode system on service upgrade
check: Any service change: all present electrodes bonded together into the grounding electrode system.
quote: shall be bonded together to form the grounding electrode system

title: Service disconnect location
check: On a panel move: disconnect readily accessible, outside or nearest the service entry, never in a bathroom.
quote: Service disconnecting means shall not be installed in bathrooms

title: Drain cleanouts accessible
check: Keep cleanouts accessible when finishing basements or adding cabinets (max 100 ft interval on horizontal drains).
cite: 2021 IRC P3005.2.1 Horizontal Drains and Building Drains
quote: Horizontal drainage pipes in buildings shall have cleanouts located at intervals of not more than 100 feet

title: Size replacement equipment by Manual J/S
check: Require a load calculation (ACCA Manual J) and equipment selection (Manual S) — not 'same size as old'.
cite: 2021 IRC M1401.3 Equipment and Appliance Sizing
quote: Heating and cooling equipment and appliances shall be sized in accordance with ACCA Manual S

title: Condensate disposal
check: AC/furnace condensate piped to an approved disposal point at 1% minimum slope.
quote: Condensate from cooling coils and evaporators shall be conveyed from the drain pan outlet to an approved place of disposal

title: Attic ventilation area
check: Net free vent area at least 1/150 of attic area (1/300 with conditions).
quote: The minimum net free ventilating area shall be 1 / 150 of the area of the vented space

title: HVAC service receptacle
check: A 15/20-A receptacle within 25 ft and on the same level as HVAC equipment, GFCI protected.
quote: The receptacle shall be located on the same level and within 25 feet (7620 mm) of the heating, air-conditioning and refrigeration equipment

title: GFCI on the HVAC service receptacle
check: The service receptacle near HVAC equipment needs GFCI.
quote: Receptacles installed in accordance with Section E3901.12 shall have ground -fault circuit-interrupter protection

title: Gas piping pressure test
check: New or altered gas piping gets inspected and pressure tested before use.
quote: all piping installations shall be visually inspected and pressure tested

title: Duct joints sealed
check: New/altered duct joints fastened and sealed (mastic, gaskets, listed tapes).
cite: 2021 IRC M1601.4.1 Joints, Seams and Connections
quote: Joints, longitudinal and transverse seams, and connections in ductwork shall be securely fastened and sealed

title: Refrigerant suction line insulated
check: Suction line insulation at least R-3, protected outdoors.
cite: 2021 IRC M1411.6 Insulation of Refrigerant Piping
quote: Piping and fittings for refrigerant vapor (suction) lines shall be insulated with insulation having a thermal resistivity of not less than R-3

title: Air sealing per energy table before insulating
check: Air barrier and sealing installed per Table N1102.4.1.1 (third-party check where required).
quote: The components of the building thermal envelope as indicated in Table N1102.4.1.1 shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions

title: Duct leakage test where required
check: Where the energy code applies, ducts are pressure tested (rough-in or post-construction).
quote: Ducts shall be pressure tested in accordance with ANSI/RESNET/ICC 380 or ASTM E1554
